Container.Name: the-desk
Container.Overview: The Desk — the morning order-sizing worksheet. Sizes each recurring buy from where a position's 30-day average sits in its 52-week range (top third 1x, middle 2x, bottom third 3x of a per-position daily base), and shows accounts, a taxable-lot LTCG exit ladder, the Monte Carlo trend against the retirement band, and the rules registry. Every displayed number traces to the payload plus a rule id; the tool never decides — all orders are hand-placed. IT SHIPS EMPTY: a first boot shows an empty wallet, which is correct rather than a misconfiguration — there is no sample data in the image and nothing is ever substituted for data you have not imported. HOW HOLDINGS GET IN: drop a custodian CSV into the inbox subdirectory of the Data path and it is read within a few minutes, then moved into inbox/imported or inbox/rejected beside it so nothing is ever consumed silently. Fidelity's Portfolio Positions export is the format understood today; a row that cannot be read is quarantined with its reason and the dashboard says so rather than importing part of a file quietly. There is deliberately NO upload button: this app has no authentication, and an unauthenticated route that writes to your wallet is one a browser on your LAN can be made to submit to. Tax lots are not present in a positions export and are not invented from one, so the LTCG ladder stays empty until a file that carries them can be ingested. IMPORTANT: the Data path (/data) now holds the wallet itself — accounts, positions, tax lots and cash flow, in a SQLite store — as well as the notifier's bookkeeping; losing that volume loses the wallet, so put it on a pool and back it up. Tape supplies market data only: set TAPE_BASE_URL plus either TAPE_CLIENT_ID/TAPE_CLIENT_SECRET or the legacy TAPE_API_KEY to price what you hold. Without Tape the wallet still renders and nothing can be sized, and the page says exactly that. NOTIFICATIONS: exactly two events — a band tier change, and a lot entering the 30-day LTCG window — and every ping is also recorded on the page under SINCE LAST LOOK, so nothing is lost if a channel is down. There are no ntfy or email settings on this template: alerting is configured once for the whole fleet in a shared file (configs/alerting.env under the Shared alerting root), which is why moving the inbox or re-pointing a topic is one edit rather than one per container — see github.com/texasdaddy/kw-common/blob/main/docs/alerting-setup.md. READ THIS BEFORE THE FIRST APPLY: this container REFUSES TO START if that file is missing, unreadable, incomplete, still carries a CHANGE-ME placeholder, or names an ntfy topic as a bare word rather than a full https URL. That is deliberate — a service that cannot alert must not come up pretending it can — and the container log names which one it was. Set the Shared alerting root and DEPLOY_ENV (prod or dev) and the first boot sends one confirmation message to prove the channel works; it is not repeated on later boots unless the shared file changes.
Container.Description: The Desk — daily order-sizing worksheet and investment-monitoring dashboard (Flask).

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: THE WALLET LIVES HERE - back it up. Holds desk.sqlite3 (your accounts, positions, tax lots and cash flow - everything the dashboard is built from) plus notifier-state.json (which tier each symbol was last seen at, and which LTCG crossings have already pinged) and the inbox/ directory you drop statements into (with imported/ and rejected/ beneath it, holding every file the container has processed). Losing this volume loses the wallet, recoverable only by importing the statements again; losing just the notifier state costs one pass with no TIER change badges and possibly one repeated LTCG ping. Through v0.2.0 this held only the bookkeeping and was cheap to lose - that is no longer true. REQUIRED - an absolute path on a POOL.

Config.Name: TAPE_BASE_URL
Config.Description: Base URL of the Tape API, e.g. https://tape.example.com (no trailing path). Needed for PRICES, which is all Tape supplies - your holdings come from the local store. Without it the container starts, serves the page and shows what you hold; no position can be sized, and the page names the variables to set rather than going blank.

Config.Name: TAPE_CLIENT_ID
Config.Description: Tape API client id (X-Client-Id), market-scoped. Register a client dedicated to The Desk via Tape's /v1/admin/clients so it can be rotated or revoked without touching anything else. Set together with TAPE_CLIENT_SECRET.

Config.Name: TAPE_CLIENT_SECRET
Config.Description: Tape API client secret (X-Client-Secret). Set together with TAPE_CLIENT_ID.

Config.Name: TAPE_API_KEY
Config.Description: LEGACY shared key (X-API-Key), used only while Tape's client registry flag is off. Prefer TAPE_CLIENT_ID/TAPE_CLIENT_SECRET. Setting both is safe — Tape ignores the key in registry mode, so the same container works either side of the cutover.

Config.Name: Shared alerting root
Config.Description: REQUIRED. The host directory holding configs/alerting.env - the ONE file every Keystone container reads for its alerting settings. Mounted READ-ONLY: this container never writes to it. Create the directory, fetch the annotated template into configs/alerting.env, chmod it 600 (it holds an SMTP password) and fill it in BEFORE you Apply - a missing or unfilled file stops this container from starting, on purpose. Full instructions: github.com/texasdaddy/kw-common/blob/main/docs/alerting-setup.md

Config.Name: DEPLOY_ENV
Config.Description: REQUIRED - type prod or dev. It selects which ntfy topic from the shared file this container publishes to (NTFY_URL_PROD or NTFY_URL_DEV) and which keys must be present. DELIBERATELY BLANK: a default here would silently put a dev deployment on the prod topic, and the symptom of that is an incident that paged the wrong place. Case does not matter.

Config.Name: SHARED_ROOT
Config.Description: The CONTAINER path the shared alerting root above is mounted at. Leave it alone - it must match the Shared alerting root mapping's container-side target, and the operator chooses only the HOST side. Change both together or neither.

Config.Name: CONFIG_PATH
Config.Description: A directory THIS container owns and writes, holding one small marker file that records the sha256 of the alerting config it last validated - which is what makes the one-time validation alert fire on a config change rather than on every restart. Defaults to a subdirectory of the Data path so there is no second volume to get wrong; it is created on first boot. NOT the alerting.env file, and never inside the shared root, which is mounted read-only.

Config.Name: TZ
Config.Description: Container timezone. Drives the notification cron below and the dates written into events. Set it to your own zone or the evening pass will fire at the wrong hour.

Config.Name: DESK_NOTIFY_CRON
Config.Description: When to run the NOTIFICATION pass, as a 5-field cron in the container's TZ. This does NOT feed the dashboard — the page is live and never waits on it. It exists because a tier CHANGE is only visible to something that was awake to see the previous tier. Default 17:30 Mon-Fri, after the close. A missed pass is not chased; the next one picks up whatever moved. USE NAMED DAYS (mon-fri), never numbers: the scheduler counts 0 as Monday, so a crontab-style 1-5 fires Tue-Sat — dropping Monday and adding a day with no close.

Config.Name: DESK_NOTIFY_ON_BOOT
Config.Description: Also run the notification pass at container start. Leave true unless you are debugging; it seeds the tier baseline so the first scheduled pass has something to compare against. It does not affect what the dashboard displays.

Config.Name: DESK_INTAKE_INTERVAL_MIN
Config.Description: How often, in minutes, to look in the Data path's inbox/ directory for a dropped statement. Also runs once at container start, so a file put there before a restart is read immediately rather than after a full interval. Set to 0 to disable the scan entirely if you would rather import by hand. This has nothing to do with prices - intake works with no Tape credentials set at all, which is the state a first install is in.

Config.Name: DESK_STALE_AMBER_HOURS
Config.Description: rule stale-1: price age at which the banner turns amber (AGING). Sizes are still shown.

Config.Name: DESK_STALE_RED_HOURS
Config.Description: rule stale-1: price age at which the banner turns red (STALE) and every computed buy size is WITHHELD — no verdict from stale data. Must be greater than the amber threshold.

Config.Name: DESK_LOG_LEVEL
Config.Description: INFO (default) or DEBUG. Credentials are never logged at any level.
